God responds to the cry of the Israelites by recognizing their suffering ('the cry of the children of Israel has come to me' and 'I have seen the oppression'), taking responsibility by commissioning Moses to lead them out of Egypt, and establishing accountability through covenant commitment ('I will be with you'). Moses is called to assume responsibility for the people's welfare and their actions in the exodus narrative. The text shows that effective leadership—whether God's or Moses'—requires awareness of the people's condition, willingness to act on their behalf, and accountability in that commitment.
